failure_reason: made.com/nl has no independent category tree left to research. Verified with curl_cffi (impersonate=chrome124/chrome131/chrome120: 403 Akamai 'Access Denied' referencing nextdirect.com; impersonate=safari17_0: 200, revealing the true behavior). With redirects disabled, every /nl/ path tested (site root /nl/, /nl/shop/storage-organisation, /nl/shop/bedding, /nl/shop/textiles/curtains) returns HTTP 301 to the exact same fixed URL: https://www.nextdirect.com/nl/nl/made - a single generic 'MADE' brand landing page on Next plc's platform (Made.com's shop was absorbed into Next after Made.com's 2022 administration; the NL storefront is now a pure redirect shell with no page-specific content of its own - all destination pages had identical byte length regardless of the source path/category slug). The only category-like structure visible on that landing page is a flat set of filter-chip links (e.g. /f/category-bedsheets, /f/category-curtains, /f/category-cushions, /f/category-throws, /f/category-towels, /f/category-bathmats, /f/category-pillowcases, /f/category-bedsets, /f/category-doormats, /f/category-chests, /f/category-dressersconsoles, /f/category-wallart, /f/category-vases, /f/category-bowls, /f/category-dinnerware, /f/category-plantpots, /f/category-glasses) which (a) live on a different domain (nextdirect.com, not made.com - out of this company's site scope), (b) are filter URLs explicitly disallowed by robots.txt's own pattern 'Disallow: */f/*category-*', and (c) carry no per-category product count on the page (only a single overall pagination for the whole brand listing, ?p=2). No genuine, rule-compliant, made.com-domain Textile or Storage category/subcategory URL with its own quantity exists to record. This is a structural finding (confirmed via direct HTTP fetch with redirects both followed and disabled), not an anti-bot wall - tier (b) Playwright (headless and headed real Chrome, both plain and with --disable-blink-features=AutomationControlled) reproduced the same 403/redirect pattern and added no new information, so escalation stopped there; tier (c) Claude-in-Chrome was unavailable (disconnected) and was not needed to reach this conclusion.
notes: ACCESS: Tier (a) direct HTTP (curl_cffi). robots.txt (www.made.com/robots.txt) is User-agent:* with no anthropic/Claude-bot naming and no blanket Disallow:/, so tier (a)/(b) were permitted; it does explicitly disallow */f/*category-* filter URLs which matches what this site's remaining links are. Chrome-impersonation (chrome124/131/120) hit a 403 Akamai edge deny page referencing nextdirect.com; Safari-impersonation (safari17_0) got HTTP 200/301 and exposed the real site behavior. With allow_redirects=False, confirmed every /nl/* path (root and multiple /shop/* category slugs) issues a 301 to the single fixed URL https://www.nextdirect.com/nl/nl/made. Tier (b) Playwright headless and headed-real-Chrome (channel=chrome, --disable-blink-features=AutomationControlled) both reproduced the 403 on the same paths, confirming the tier (a) finding rather than revealing new content; both tiers exhausted before reaching tier (c), which was disconnected anyway (list_connected_browsers empty per task brief) so no fallback was available or needed. TREE: made.com/nl has been decommissioned as an independent multi-category storefront; it is a pure 301-redirect shell into a single fixed Next plc brand-listing page on a different domain (nextdirect.com), so no mega-menu, sitemap-listed category page, or sub-nav strip resolves to distinct, made.com-hosted content (robots.txt's own Sitemap: entry, https://www.made.com/sitemap-index.xml, lists only GB-EN category/product sitemaps - no NL-specific sitemap exists, and the GB /shop/* URLs listed there also now 301-redirect the same way under Safari impersonation). QTY: not obtainable - no per-category listing page or count exists on the made.com domain to read a number from. EXCLUDED: all destination content, since it resolves outside made.com's own domain (nextdirect.com/nl/nl/made and nextdirect.com/nl/nl/brands/madecom) and only via disallowed /f/*category-* filter-chip URLs - both facts independently disqualify it under the URL rules (no filter/collection URLs, no cross-domain URL substitution, no invented URLs). No textile_rows or storage_rows recorded; both arrays are empty by design, not by omission. Sister site Made.com UK (SR48) reported the same Akamai wall pattern at tiers a/b and partially recovered some rows via tier (c) before that Chrome session disconnected mid-task; this NL run had no tier (c) available at all, and independently confirmed via direct fetch (redirects disabled) that the underlying site structure itself no longer has distinct category pages to recover even if a browser tier had been available.
